wholePhysicalScope: The named OpenStreetMap site encloses the whole heritage complex. The Pakistan Department of Archaeology and Museums provides the geographic point used to place the stupa. Printed scale and compass establish the terrace and adjacent chapel layout.
lodDetails: Four levels retain the broken drum and outer processional terrace.
limitations: Draft exterior: approximate photographic proportions and simplified ornament. It is not a survey, photogrammetric reconstruction or approved current geographic replacement.
Plates IV and IX of the 1918 guide establish the ground plan and rough damaged limestone drum and immediate masonry. The Taxila Museum specifies the 131 ft drum diameter and 45 ft surviving height.
Terrain sampling/contact, geographic alignment and site activation remain pending. Runtime LODs are produced by the registered after-import pipeline and require visual review.
Reference photos remain in the local Qualla corpus; only provenance, paths and hashes are retained here.
